questions.question: Which TCP port is commonly used for Secure Shell (SSH) remote administrative access?
questions.explanation: SSH operates primarily on TCP port 22 to provide encrypted remote login and command-line execution.

questions.question: What is the standard TCP port number used for Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS)?
questions.explanation: HTTPS uses TCP port 443 to secure web traffic using TLS/SSL encryption.

questions.question: Which port number is standard for Domain Name System (DNS) queries and name resolution?
questions.explanation: DNS uses port 53 for both TCP (zone transfers) and UDP (standard name resolution queries).

questions.question: Which ports are used by Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) for server and client communications respectively?
questions.explanation: DHCP server listens on UDP port 67, and DHCP client listens on UDP port 68.

questions.question: Which TCP port is assigned to Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) for connecting to Windows desktops?
questions.explanation: RDP uses TCP port 3389 (and sometimes UDP 3389) for remote graphical desktop access.

questions.question: What is the standard TCP port for unencrypted web traffic using HTTP?
questions.explanation: HTTP uses TCP port 80 for standard web page transmission in clear text.

questions.question: Which TCP port is used by FTP for control commands and session management?
questions.explanation: FTP control channel uses TCP port 21, whereas the data channel uses TCP port 20.

questions.question: Which TCP port is used for data transfer in traditional File Transfer Protocol (FTP)?
questions.explanation: FTP data transmission takes place over TCP port 20.

questions.question: Which protocol and port number are used for legacy, unencrypted remote terminal connections?
questions.explanation: Telnet uses TCP port 23 and transmits all data, including passwords, in clear text.

questions.question: What is the standard TCP port used for Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) to send emails?
questions.explanation: SMTP uses TCP port 25 for mail routing and outgoing email transmissions.

questions.question: Which TCP port is used by Post Office Protocol version 3 (POP3) to download emails from a mail server?
questions.explanation: POP3 uses TCP port 110 for retrieving mail messages.

questions.question: Which TCP port is utilized by Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP) for syncing emails?
questions.explanation: IMAP uses TCP port 143 to manage and sync mailboxes across devices.

questions.question: What is the primary TCP port used for Server Message Block (SMB) for Windows file and printer sharing?
questions.explanation: Modern SMB (without NetBIOS) operates directly over TCP port 445.

questions.question: Which UDP ports are standard for Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) agent queries and traps?
questions.explanation: SNMP queries use UDP port 161, and SNMP traps use UDP port 162.

questions.question: Which port is used for Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) queries?
questions.explanation: LDAP communicates over TCP/UDP port 389.

questions.question: What is the standard port for secure LDAP (LDAPS) running over TLS/SSL?
questions.explanation: LDAPS uses TCP/UDP port 636 for encrypted directory service communications.

questions.question: Which UDP port is used for Network Time Protocol (NTP) synchronization?
questions.explanation: NTP uses UDP port 123 to synchronize clocks across network devices.

questions.question: Which UDP port is standard for Trivial File Transfer Protocol (TFTP), often used for firmware updates?
questions.explanation: TFTP is a lightweight file transfer protocol running on UDP port 69 without session security or authentication.

questions.question: What protocol and port are used for secure email retrieval via IMAPS?
questions.explanation: IMAPS (IMAP over SSL/TLS) uses TCP port 993.

questions.question: What port is designated for secure email retrieval using POP3S?
questions.explanation: POP3S (POP3 over SSL/TLS) operates on TCP port 995.

questions.question: Which TCP/UDP port is associated with the Kerberos authentication protocol?
questions.explanation: Kerberos authentication utilizes TCP and UDP port 88.

questions.question: Which TCP port is commonly used for MySQL database connections?
questions.explanation: MySQL database communication uses TCP port 3306 by default.

questions.question: What is the standard TCP port for Microsoft SQL Server database engine?
questions.explanation: Microsoft SQL Server listens on TCP port 1433 by default.

questions.question: Which ports are used by Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) for VoIP call setup and signaling?
questions.explanation: SIP uses port 5060 for cleartext and port 5061 for encrypted (TLS) VoIP signaling.

questions.question: Which TCP port is used for Apple Filing Protocol (AFP) file sharing?
questions.explanation: Apple Filing Protocol (AFP) communicates over TCP port 548.

questions.question: Which port is used by Service Location Protocol (SLP) for discovering network services?
questions.explanation: SLP uses TCP/UDP port 427 for device and service discovery.

questions.question: Which NetBIOS service uses TCP port 139 for session management?
questions.explanation: NetBIOS Session Service operates on TCP port 139.

questions.question: Which of the following protocols is used primarily to resolve domain names to IP addresses and operates on port 53?
questions.explanation: DNS (Domain Name System) handles name resolution on port 53.

questions.question: An administrator needs to securely manage a Linux server over the network without exposing credentials in plaintext. Which port should be allowed through the firewall?
questions.explanation: TCP port 22 is used for SSH, which provides secure, encrypted administrative access.

questions.question: Which of the following ports should be blocked at the network perimeter firewall to prevent unencrypted remote terminal access vulnerabilities?
questions.explanation: Port 23 is Telnet, which transmits data unencrypted and should be disabled or blocked in favor of SSH.

questions.question: Which of the following protocols rely primarily on UDP rather than TCP? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: DNS, DHCP, and NTP use UDP for fast, connectionless packet transmission (though DNS can use TCP for zone transfers).

questions.question: Which of the following protocols use TCP for reliable, connection-oriented data delivery? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: HTTP (80), HTTPS (443), and SSH (22) all operate over TCP. TFTP operates over UDP.

questions.question: A technician troubleshooting an email delivery issue notes that outgoing mail isn't reaching the destination server. Which port should be checked on the mail server firewall?
questions.explanation: Port 25 is used for SMTP, which handles outgoing email transmission between mail servers.

questions.question: Which port pairing correctly represents the control and data channels for traditional FTP?
questions.explanation: FTP uses port 21 for control commands and port 20 for data transfer.

questions.question: What is the primary function of TCP port 3389 in an enterprise IT environment?
questions.explanation: TCP port 3389 is standard for Microsoft Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP).

questions.question: Which protocol pairs with TCP port 445 to facilitate file and printer sharing in modern Windows networks?
questions.explanation: Server Message Block (SMB) runs on TCP port 445 for Windows file sharing.

questions.question: Which of the following ports are associated with secure variants of web and directory services? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Port 443 (HTTPS) and Port 636 (LDAPS) are secure versions of HTTP and LDAP respectively.

questions.question: Why is UDP preferred over TCP for DHCP and DNS standard lookups?
options: A) UDP provides encryption by default.
B) UDP offers faster, connectionless communication without overhead.
C) UDP guarantees packet delivery order.
questions.explanation: UDP is connectionless and lightweight, making it ideal for fast queries and address assignment where speed outweighs guaranteed reliability.

questions.question: An IT technician is configuring a firewall for a secure web server. Which port must be open to allow encrypted web traffic?
questions.explanation: Port 443 handles HTTPS traffic, which encrypts web data using TLS.

questions.question: Which of the following email protocols download messages and typically delete them from the server by default?
questions.explanation: POP3 (Port 110) downloads emails locally, whereas IMAP syncs mail across multiple devices while keeping copies on the server.

questions.question: Which port number is utilized by LDAP for unencrypted directory lookups?
questions.explanation: LDAP runs on TCP/UDP port 389 in cleartext.

questions.question: Which protocol uses UDP port 123 to ensure network devices have synchronized system clocks?
questions.explanation: NTP (Network Time Protocol) operates on UDP port 123 for time synchronization.

questions.question: Which of the following ports are used for network device monitoring and management via SNMP? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: SNMP uses UDP port 161 for requests/responses and UDP port 162 for traps.

questions.question: Which TCP port is used by PostgreSQL database servers by default?
questions.explanation: PostgreSQL uses TCP port 5432.

questions.question: What is the standard TCP port for Oracle database communication?
questions.explanation: Oracle databases typically listen on TCP port 1521.

questions.question: Which of the following protocols are categorized as remote terminal or desktop access tools? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: SSH, Telnet, and RDP are remote access protocols. SMTP is used for email.

questions.question: When configuring a firewall to allow secure remote management of a server via command line, which port should be opened?
questions.explanation: Port 22 is SSH, which provides secure command-line remote management.

questions.question: Which of the following secure mail protocols use TCP port 993 and TCP port 995 respectively?
questions.explanation: IMAPS operates on TCP port 993, and POP3S operates on TCP port 995.
